Affirmative responses from configured nonvoters cannot substitute for the voter support needed to confirm authority.

grounding.derivation: The API promises to ensure this peer is still leader and identifies stale reads after lost leadership as its use. Developer documentation identifies voters as confirmation recipients. Configuration semantics separate voter authority from nonvoting replication. Therefore a node already superseded by a newer-term voter-majority leader cannot honestly confirm its authority during a wholly later invocation; nonvoter acknowledgements do not supply that authority. Source observations identify a possible failure path but do not establish its reachability or result.
grounding.applicability: Correct stable-membership run with actual elected newer leader before invocation and no reconnection during verification. This is a safety requirement, not a requirement to complete within a finite timeout.
unresolved: The controlled history and actual completion outcome have not yet been executed.
alternatives: Voter lease expiration or higher-term rejection may correctly cause verification failure; that is not a violation.

materials.text:
## Operations

### Leader Write

Most write operations must be performed on the leader.

* RequestConfigChange - update the raft peer list configuration
* Apply - apply a log entry to the log on a majority of peers, and the FSM. See [raft apply](apply.md) for more details.
* Barrier - a special Apply that does not modify the FSM, used to wait for previous logs to be applied
* LeadershipTransfer - stop accepting client requests, and tell a different peer to start a leadership election
* Restore (Snapshot) - overwrite the cluster state with the contents of the snapshot (excluding cluster configuration)
* VerifyLeader - send a heartbeat to all voters to confirm the peer is still the leader

after.execution_owner: commitment mutex; Raft main-loop commit channel consumer
after.protocol_context: One leader tracker and its latest voter set
after.trigger: match or setConfiguration recalculates majority index; notification wakes leader loop
implementation_guards: Only current voter IDs are recorded; match values increase monotonically.
Quorum index must reach startIndex before commitment advances.
writes: Set commitment index and notify; main loop updates Raft commit index and committed configuration, then processes inflight prefix.

cross_activity_effects.A5: Committed inflight prefix is queued to FSM processing.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Committed removal of local voter triggers shutdown or follower transition.

after.execution_owner: Raft main loop and per-peer replicators
after.protocol_context: Active leader term and current configuration
after.trigger: Apply admission or leader no-op/configuration dispatch
writes: Assign index and term, enqueue inflight, persist logs, then credit local match and notify replicators.
Successful append responses update nextIndex and report last sent entry to the captured commitment tracker.
important_branches: Local store error fails futures and sets Follower.
Rejection backs nextIndex down; missing retained logs switches to snapshot transfer; newer response term signals stepdown.
CommitTimeout sends ordinary replication even without new commands; separate heartbeats carry no commit index.
async_boundaries: Network request/response and optional pipeline run outside main loop.

after.execution_owner: Raft main loop; per-peer vote RPC goroutines
after.protocol_context: Latest voter configuration and one election attempt
after.trigger: Follower contact timeout starts candidacy; pre-vote or transfer bypass precedes electSelf
implementation_guards: Only configured voters are solicited; each attempt has its own reply channel.
Vote recipient checks candidate eligibility, known leader, term, log freshness and persisted prior vote.
A higher returned term ends candidacy; election timeout creates a new attempt.
writes: Persist current term and vote before including self support; majority of grants sets Leader.
async_boundaries: Replies to abandoned election channels are not consumed by new attempts.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Acquired leadership permits entry creation but fresh commitment still requires a current-term entry.

unknowns: StableStore partial write/crash semantics for the separately persisted vote term and candidate remain unread.

after.protocol_context: Incoming leader term and local retained log/snapshot
after.trigger: AppendEntries through normal RPC or heartbeat dispatch
implementation_guards: Reject old term; newer term or ordinary non-follower state transitions to follower.
Check previous index/term; delete conflicting suffix before storing replacement entries.
writes: Revert latest configuration to committed when truncating through latest configuration.
On success set commit index to min(leader commit index, local last index), update committed configuration and process prefix.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Append request changes term/state and known leader before log matching.
cross_activity_effects.A4: Accepted configuration entries update latest/committed metadata.

unknowns: Whether producer backtracking and transport ordering always prevent follower commitment beyond the prefix established by this request.
After successful suffix deletion followed by StoreLogs error, cached last-log metadata is left unchanged; supported fault recovery remains unresolved.

after.execution_owner: Raft main loop queues work; runFSM serially invokes application
after.protocol_context: Ordered commit tuples and restore requests
after.trigger: processLogs of newly committed prefix; FSM mutation channel
writes: Read each unapplied log, queue commands/barriers/configurations as applicable, and advance lastApplied after queueing.
FSM Apply/ApplyBatch returns responses before their futures complete; barriers are acknowledged in ordered FSM work.
important_branches: No-op logs need no FSM mutation.
Restore serially replaces FSM and local FSM indices.

cross_activity_effects.A7: Apply completion is distinct from commit and from main-loop lastApplied queue position.

after.trigger: runLeader creates fresh commitment, inflight list, replication map and channels; exit cleans up
writes: First no-op establishes startIndex entry.
Cleanup stops old workers, fails remaining inflight and verify futures, and clears active leader state.
important_branches: New-term RPC or replication stale-term signal and failed voter lease can force follower state.
Old workers retain their original commitment and stepDown channels, not a new term tracker.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Fresh per-term match accounting prevents old replication replies from qualifying new-term decisions.
cross_activity_effects.A7: Leadership loss errors leave uncertain command commitment, as documented by Apply.

after.protocol_context: Latest and committed configurations with their log indices
after.trigger: Stable configuration channel admits membership change; follower/new-start scan consumes configuration logs
implementation_guards: Admission requires prior configuration committed and this leader current-term entry committed.
Configuration validation requires unique nonempty IDs/addresses and at least one voter; prevIndex guards stale caller updates.
writes: New latest configuration immediately changes commitment voter map and starts/stops replication; existing retained voter matches survive setConfiguration.

cross_activity_effects.A2: Latest voters control election participation and lease quorum; nonvoters still receive replication.

after.execution_owner: Raft initialization or main RPC loop, FSM goroutine
writes: Startup restores term and last log, tries snapshots newest first, restores configuration, then scans suffix for configuration entries.
InstallSnapshot checks term/version/size, finalizes snapshot, waits for FSM restore, updates applied/snapshot indices and configuration, then compacts logs.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Successful snapshot response credits sender match index.
cross_activity_effects.A2: Installed snapshot term can force follower state.
cross_activity_effects.A6: Monotonic stores remove old logs; other stores compact with trailing retention.

unknowns: Delayed same-term snapshots versus already applied state need further history analysis.

after.execution_owner: Leader main loop and FSM goroutine
implementation_guards: Reject unsupported version or outstanding configuration change; wait for FSM restore and panic on restore failure.
writes: Abort inflight commands; use current configuration and term with a newly burned higher index; set last log, applied and snapshot indices.

cross_activity_effects.A1: Index gap forces future replication to transfer snapshot rather than replay old data.

after.execution_owner: Snapshot goroutine with main-loop configuration query and FSM snapshot callback
after.protocol_context: Applied FSM position and committed configuration
implementation_guards: Reject snapshot position earlier than committed configuration index; persist and close before updating stable snapshot metadata and compacting.
writes: Snapshot stores applied index/term and committed configuration; compaction retains configured trailing logs.

cross_activity_effects.A3: Snapshots supply restart and lagging follower reconstruction.

after.execution_owner: Raft main loop, replication workers, verifyFuture vote mutex
after.protocol_context: One VerifyLeader future while node remains in leader loop
after.trigger: API submits future; first leader-loop visit calls verifyLeader
implementation_guards: Threshold derives from voter-only quorumSize; initializes one self vote.
Future notification is emitted once; failure votes cause early stepdown and error; leader cleanup fails remaining futures.
writes: Registers future in every replication worker without checking suffrage.
Worker drains its notification set and supplies bool support; future counter contains no voter identity or eligibility field.
Second main-loop visit responds nil when votes reach threshold.

cross_activity_effects.A7: Successful future is exposed as leadership verification for avoiding stale FSM reads.

unknowns: Can nonvoter responses complete verification without fresh voter quorum support under a legal partition schedule before lease stepdown?
Does contract require voter quorum confirmation per call, or is stronger stale-read endpoint history necessary to attribute a failure?

formation.explanation: Leader assigns term/index, stores locally and replicates to all configured peers. Successful append or snapshot responses report match indices to the leader-term tracker. Only configured voters contribute to its majority, and the majority index must reach the first current-term entry. The main loop consumes commit notifications, updates committed configuration and queues the committed prefix. Followers validate previous log context, repair conflicting suffixes, accept leader commit propagation and queue their prefix. runFSM serializes actual application and responds to local futures afterward; queue position alone is not completion.

context.explanation: Follower timeout can start a voter election. Optional pre-vote precedes durable term increment and persisted self vote. Requests are scoped to one election reply channel; recipient eligibility, freshness, leader and prior-vote checks constrain grants. Majority establishes leadership. Higher terms, failed voter lease, replication stale-term signal or committed local removal end authority. Leader exit stops workers and fails pending work; new leadership creates a fresh commitment object and no-op. Transfer catches up a selected peer then sends TimeoutNow; it bypasses pre-vote and temporarily prevents new leader client work.

connection.explanation: Election log freshness preserves prior eligible history, while committing a new-term no-op establishes the new leader commitment boundary. Old election reply channels and old replication commitment objects remain separate from new attempts/terms. Latest logged configuration controls election and quorum membership before its commitment, but a further configuration requires prior configuration and current-term entry commitment. Conflicting follower suffix removal restores committed membership; snapshots restore configuration and applied prefix before suffix scanning or resumed participation. Already queued committed work remains FSM work across role change, while uncommitted leader futures become uncertain errors. VerifyLeader is a separate authority consumer using replication notifications; its voter-derived threshold and all-peer registration require eligibility investigation.

open_details: Transport-specific dispatch/order and cancellation contracts remain to be read before constructing schedules.
Storage partial failures and crash recovery atomicity remain unresolved.
Verification nonvoter eligibility is a sourced discrepancy, not an established violation.
after.rationale: Both formation and authority paths and their old-work handling have been traced with support for configuration, persistence, recovery and application; deeper local premises remain explicit.

after.meaning: Raft records a commit-index prefix for processing; this alone does not say that the FSM has applied it.
after.validity_context: Leader majority calculation or follower accepted leader commit propagation in its term/log context.
after.durability: Volatile index; log and snapshot retain history.
after.recovery: Startup restores snapshot applied position; subsequent consensus propagates commit knowledge.

after.meaning: Tracker records the greatest reported replicated log index for each presently included voter.
after.validity_context: Only voter IDs in this tracker configuration; reported persistence is inferred from local store completion or successful peer response.
after.durability: Volatile tracker; underlying peer logs are separately persisted.
after.recovery: Recreated with zero match indices on each leader term.

after.meaning: Node has recorded its current protocol term after persisting that term to StableStore.
after.validity_context: Local current term; does not alone confer leadership.
after.durability: Persisted before local field update; failure panics.
after.recovery: NewRaft loads the stable current term before starting goroutines.

after.meaning: Verification future has counted self and affirmative replication notifications up to its voter-derived numeric threshold.
after.validity_context: One future registered while leader; counted notifications do not themselves retain peer suffrage or term.
after.recovery: No recovery; leader exit fails pending tracked futures.

What atomicity/recovery assumptions connect separately persisted vote term and candidate after an interrupted write?
Why does authority verification register nonvoters although threshold and lease use only voters?
